question:
After each change to a system, how should the team decide what to test again, and at which point of the process?

Answer with a list of guidelines. After each guideline, cite the source it comes from: the path of the SWEBOK file if you have it, otherwise a verbatim quote of at least 8 words from the passage, in the form (source: ...).
answer:
# Summary

After each system change, teams should determine what to retest by conducting impact analysis to identify affected areas, selecting and prioritizing test cases accordingly, and performing regression testing at appropriate process stages—from unit to integration to deployment—using automation where possible to ensure timely detection of unintended effects.

# Guidelines

- Perform regression testing after each modification to verify that changes [SWEBOK excerpt 9719b1133051fb8e8d26] system still complies with specified requirements; apply test case selection, minimization, and prioritization to manage the scope. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Testing Levels, Objectives, and Approaches/Alpha, Beta, and Regression Testing Procedures.md)

- Conduct regression testing at each test level (unit, integration, system, etc.), and perform it typically [SWEBOK excerpt 0f6027292d0f7e6a203b]. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Testing Levels, Objectives, and Approaches/Regression Testing in Software Development.md)

- Use traceability links among requirements, design, code, and test cases to trace affected elements and establish the footprint of work needed when a change occurs, guiding what must be retested. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Requirements Management, Quality, and Testing Practices/Requirements Traceability and Change Impact Analysis/Traceability in Software Requirements and Design.md)

- Perform impact analysis to identify all systems and products affected by a change request, then use that knowledge to determine the testing needed to validate the modification. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Testing, Operations, and Maintenance/Software Operations and Maintenance Practices/Impact Analysis in Software Maintenance.md)

- In continuous integration and DevOps, perform regression testing continuously with each integration [SWEBOK excerpt c4851070e003114eb8a1] use smoke testing to guarantee the system is testable before release. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Testing, Operations, and Maintenance/Testing Across Development Processes and Domains/Testing Strategies Across Methodologies and Domains/Test Automation and Domain-Specific Testing Approaches.md)

- Use regression testing tools to [SWEBOK excerpt 4e31a19101591ba0b19b], and use tools that [SWEBOK excerpt 79bda116780c66bfd000]. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Testing, Operations, and Maintenance/Software Operations and Maintenance Practices/Software Testing Tools and Standards/Software Testing Tools and Techniques/Software Testing and Reliability Evaluation Tools.md)

- Plan and execute test activities during maintenance requests processing; [SWEBOK excerpt 0053a8303c0cf7a4bae1] appropriate tests—regression testing is especially important in maintenance. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Testing, Operations, and Maintenance/Software Operations and Maintenance Practices/Software Maintenance_ Technical, Management, and Comprehension Challenges/Software Comprehension and Testing in Maintenance.md)

- In Agile processes, manage the risk of regression defects and the impact of changing requirements on test artifacts as explicit objectives of the testing process. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Testing, Operations, and Maintenance/Testing Across Development Processes and Domains/Testing Strategies Across Methodologies and Domains/Testing Techniques Across Development Levels and Shift-Left Approaches.md)

- Determine integration test points by deciding the sequence in which components are integrated and specifying [SWEBOK excerpt e3f413ae4d998da1b8a0]. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Construction Techniques and Practices/Integration Strategies and Planning/Integration During Software Construction.md)

- Coordinate continuous testing [SWEBOK excerpt a3bf4affce14a7425dbf] to evaluate quality at every step of the [SWEBOK excerpt d7e57d9d89af6c96b337]. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Maintenance, Evolution, and Quality Assurance/Continuous Integration, Delivery, and Software Maintenance/Continuous Delivery and Testing in Software Development.md)

- Balance [SWEBOK excerpt eac9e9b4ff99102e4f0c] against the resources required, as this trade-off can be significant given the many tests that might need to be executed. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Testing Levels, Objectives, and Approaches/Alpha, Beta, and Regression Testing Procedures.md)

- Maintain and update test repositories so that changes to software requirements or design are reflected in changes to the tests, enabling reuse of test cases after modifications. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Testing Methodologies and Quality Assurance Practices/Software Testing Techniques, Measurement, and Management/Test Completion and Knowledge Management/Test Completion and Artifact Reusability in Software Testing.md)
